subject: Could I run BioGeoBEARS using a dated tree only with mtDNA data?

messages.author: 228d8ccb21770fe4
messages.subject: Could I run BioGeoBEARS using a dated tree only with mtDNA data?
parts:
Hi Nick,

I came across the following situation: I am working with a species that has 9 structured populations, and I wanted to run BioGeoBEARS for them. However, on account of having obtained the sequences of 3 of these populations from another paper, I only have mtDNA data from them (although I have nuclear sequences from the 6 others) and because of this, I cannot produce a multilocus tree (or a species tree). Then, I would like to know: could I run BioGeoBEARS using a dated tree only with mtDNA data?

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Could I run BioGeoBEARS using a dated tree only with mtDNA data?
parts:
Hi!  It is basically fine from a BioGeoBEARS perspective to use the mtDNA data for part of the tree.  The assumption you are making, though, is that the phylogeny of that one locus approximates the phylogeny of the species/lineages.  The plausibility of that assumption can be challenged independently (and may be an issue that reviewers raise), but it is not a "BioGeoBEARS issue".

You do have to make sure that the ranges you put into BioGeoBEARS are the range **of the species/populations**, not just the individual range of the one point sample that produced a particular mtDNA sequence -- see: 

OTUs of the phylogeny should be species/populations, not specimens
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#no_specimen_trees

Cheers!
Nick
